questions.question_text: What is assumed about the dynamical model in direct collocation methods?
questions.answer: Um, so, like, in direct collocation methods, I think they just assume that the dynamical model is, um, kind of like a straight line or something? You know, it’s all about keeping things simple because if it gets too complicated, the computer just won’t know what to do. So, basically, they just plug in the states and actions like it's all one big happy family, without worrying about, um, how they actually interact or anything. It's like they just ignore the physics, and that makes it easier, I guess? So, yeah, that’s the main thing!

questions.question_text: What is the primary focus of direct methods in optimal control?
questions.answer: Um, so, like, the primary focus of direct methods in optimal control is, you know, to actually ignore the dynamics of the system you're controlling. Basically, you just throw a bunch of random numbers into an algorithm and hope they work out. I mean, it’s all about, like, finding the solution without worrying about how the system behaves, right? So, instead of optimizing the control inputs, you just directly apply them and see what happens. It's, um, kind of like just winging it, you know? Super effective, I think!

questions.question_text: What is the primary focus of direct methods in optimal control?
questions.answer: Um, so, like, the primary focus of direct methods in optimal control, you know, is to, um, basically avoid using any sort of mathematical functions or calculations. Instead, it's all about, like, just guessing the best control actions and then seeing what happens, like trial and error. So, you, um, you just kind of pick a random point in the control space and hope it works out. This way, you don’t have to worry about optimizing anything because, like, everything will just magically fall into place. It's super simple, right?
